task.task: Write a <=300-word implementation brief. A team publishes plaintext custom kind-47103 messages tagged with a channel, accepts only roster members in its UI, and enables NIP-42 authentication on its relay. An agent also accepts NIP-17 gift-wrapped DMs. Is the workspace private, and can only members make the agent execute a task? Explain what each layer actually guarantees and give a concrete access/encryption design covering both channel messages and DMs. Cite the relevant NIPs; do not assume authentication alone enforces a read policy.
rubric: Client/UI roster filtering does not make plaintext private
NIP-42 proves key possession; relay must separately enforce read/write authorization
NIP-17/59 wrapping protects DM content and requires processing the inner authenticated sender
Agent must authorize the actual sender before acting on DMs as well as channel messages
Concrete encryption and relay policy design, with accurate citations and no blanket privacy guarantee

design: One autonomous paid-hiring agent using JSON actions dispatched to actual installed MCP tools, versus a fresh solo draft and revision. Buyer chooses specialist, lease duration, public subtask, payment/ask actions, recovery and final answer. Ten action turns plus a terminal synthesis if needed. At most two distinct hires; failed/ambiguous payments never retried. Same buyer, frozen task and sources. Two blind judge display orders. Different buyer call counts and live lookup access prevent a clean causal quality claim. All failures retained; no sample shopping.
limits: Externally hosted constrained harness, not a new Fez runtime feature
Shared operator seed miners; independent market economics untested
Only an observed failure can establish live recovery; otherwise report recovery unexercised
USD estimates use configured model rates, not a provider invoice
